verdict.rationale: Proa uses an islands model. It emits server-rendered HTML plus only the JavaScript each interactive island needs, and each hydrated island gets a small vanilla-JS module and seed state on a shared runtime of about 1.3 KB gzipped. Static components can ship no JS at all, and Suspense streams ready chunks out of order so slow data does not block the page. This covers the core of selective, incremental hydration for faster interactivity, though the evidence comes from first-party docs and the repo only. Missing for 10: documented hydration scheduling or priority strategies (e.g. on-visible or idle hydration), evidence that islands hydrate as streamed chunks arrive, independent or hands-on corroboration of time-to-interactive gains.
